title: Discrimination in job postings and selection
summary: The law of May 10, 2007 protects candidates from the job posting stage. Selection criteria must respect anti-discrimination rules and reasonable accommodation requirements.
body: Article 5, § 2, notably addresses job postings, access conditions, and recruitment criteria. Protected criteria under Article 4 include notably age, sexual orientation, beliefs, language, health status, disability, and social origin or condition. The federal scope reserves competencies of Communities and Regions.

Article 14 prohibits direct and indirect discrimination, orders to discriminate, harassment, and refusal of reasonable accommodations for a person with a disability. It also covers cumulative and intersectional discrimination. Plan a procedure to adapt selection tests.

Justifications vary by criterion. Article 8 frames essential and determining professional requirements; Article 12 provides a special regime for age. A client preference does not exempt the recruiter from checking these conditions.

title: Gender equality from job posting
summary: The Gender law of May 10, 2007 applies to job postings, selection criteria, and pay. Pregnancy or family responsibilities cannot be used to reject an application.
body: Article 4 notably protects sex, pregnancy, medically assisted reproduction, motherhood, family responsibilities, gender identity and expression, sexual characteristics, and medical or social transition. Article 6, § 2, explicitly covers job postings and pay setting.

Article 13 limits direct sex-based distinctions to essential and determining professional requirements under legal conditions. Describe actual tasks and constraints rather than seeking a man or woman for stereotyped reasons.

For writing, the guide from the Institute for Gender Equality, September 2025 edition, recommends neutral titles and M/F/X mention. For a posting with M/F/X, apply these neutrality principles. This mention does not replace non-discriminatory selection. Guide verified: https://igvm-iefh.belgium.be/fr/documentation/egalite-dacces-lemploi-informations-et-conseils-pratiques-pour-les-employeurs

title: Origin and nationality in recruitment
summary: The law of July 30, 1981 prohibits racial discrimination in access to employment. The recruiter must also refuse discriminatory instructions from a client.
body: Articles 4 and 5 cover nationality, presumed race, skin color, ancestry, and national or ethnic origin, as well as job postings and recruitment criteria. Check work eligibility without transforming this check into a general preference for an origin.

Article 12 notably prohibits direct, indirect discrimination and orders to discriminate. For racial criteria other than nationality, Article 8 strictly frames essential and determining professional requirements; nationality-related justifications notably fall under Article 7.

An apparently neutral requirement must also be examined for its effects. Requiring a language skill useful for the position rather than an origin or mother tongue avoids a filter that may indirectly exclude some candidates.

title: CCT No. 38: recruitment and selection
summary: CCT No. 38 frames costs, documents, and equal treatment. It also contains conduct rules on job posting content, privacy, and confidentiality.
body: Articles 2 bis to 6 notably provide for equal treatment, assumption of employer-ordered tests, and prohibition of certified copies. An ordinary copy suffices; the original may be presented in case of doubt. Article 4 provides a certificate on request for the candidate subject to unemployment check.

Chapter IV distinguishes signatories' commitments regarding conduct rules. Article 8 lists the position, requirements, location unless impossible, any recruitment reservation, and application method. Article 9 provides for a written response within a reasonable time to candidates meeting requirements but not retained.

Articles 11 and 12 limit personal questions to what is relevant for the position and provide for confidentiality. Article 7 commits signatories to promote these rules among their members. Coordinated version last modified by CCT No. 38 sexies, effective October 10, 2008.

title: Practical tests and interview questions
summary: The SPF Employment reminds of the limits of hiring tests and personal questions. The test must only assess competencies needed for the position.
body: The SPF clarifies that a selection test does not by itself create a contract and should not be paid. However, its duration cannot exceed what is necessary to assess competency. This rule does not allow ordinary work to be performed under the guise of selection.
The costs of tests ordered by the employer are borne by the employer. Travel remains in principle the candidate's responsibility, but the procedure must limit it as much as possible.

Questions about private life must relate to the nature and conditions of the position. Pregnancy does not normally come up in the interview; legally dangerous situations for the mother or child require specific treatment respecting equality. Undated page: the date used corresponds to the last CCT No. 38 modification cited.

title: Replace native language requirement
summary: Unia analyzes the native language requirement as a risk of indirect discrimination based on national or ethnic origin. Describe the language level required for tasks.
body: The opinion notably targets mentions of 'native French speaker' and 'English native speaker'. They use a characteristic tied to origin background rather than actual language mastery and may exclude people with necessary competencies.

The recruiter must tie language requirements to actual work and evaluate the competency level needed. Unia clarifies that its analysis focuses on national or ethnic origin, as its mandate does not directly cover language criterion. The opinion is dated January 1, 2017.

title: Age limits in job postings
summary: Unia reminds that an age limit in a posting must be justified. Seek a specific skill rather than an age range.
body: A posting limited to an age range or an instruction given to a temporary agency directly excludes other candidates. The page recalls that a limit without legitimate, appropriate, and reasonable reason is prohibited.

Unia distinguishes limits provided by a legal arrangement, such as certain conditions of a first employment agreement. Verify the applicable arrangement before adopting a limit in the posting; exceptions do not permit a general age filter.
The sheet refers to the anti-discrimination law of May 10, 2007 and its special age justification regime. Undated page: the date used is the entry into force of that law, June 9, 2007.

title: Candidate data and reference checks
summary: The DPA asks to limit data collected to position needs. References, sensitive data, and criminal records are not freely checked.
body: Tailor the questionnaire to the function. Political opinions, beliefs, and union memberships are sensitive data, in principle protected against processing. Questions about desire for children or pregnancy are normally excluded.

To contact a former employer or client, the DPA requires prior candidate information and free and sufficiently precise authorization. A reference listed in the CV may serve as agreement for that reference. A refusal to consent should not automatically halt selection.

Criminal history is subject to a special regime. A legal professional obligation may justify checking; consent is insufficient. The DPA advises against keeping the extract after verification without legal need. Undated page: reference date used is GDPR entry into force, May 24, 2016, applicable from May 25, 2018.

title: Medical examinations at hiring
summary: The law of January 28, 2003 limits medical investigation to current fitness and position characteristics. The recruiter cannot organize general medical screening.
body: Article 2 covers candidates in both private and public sectors. Article 3, § 1, frames tests, exams, and questions intended to gather medical or hereditary information. It notably prohibits predictive genetic tests and HIV screening, subject to regulatory exceptions in Article 5.

Article 3, § 2, provides for information by confidential registered letter ten days before the exam, concerning information sought, the exam, and its reasons. Under § 3, only competent occupational health doctors can request or perform these exams.

The employer and candidate receive the decision via the medical form provided. Written justification of unfitness is transmitted to the doctor designated by the person involved. Article 4 requires informing of conditions susceptible to being worsened by the position. Date used: publication in the Belgian Official Journal of April 9, 2003.

title: When to organize preliminary health assessment
summary: Medical surveillance depends on position risks. For a covered position, preliminary assessment must occur before actual assignment.
body: Title 4 of Book I of the Wellbeing Code frames health surveillance. Risk analysis, with the occupational health doctor and intervention of the competent committee, determines covered positions. Screen work does not automatically require mandatory surveillance.

Under Article I.4-26, assessment may precede contract signature if it constitutes the final selection step and the contract actually results when the candidate is declared fit. It may also follow signature but must precede risk exposure.

Article I.4-13 prohibits additional exams outside the provided framework. Fitness is assessed for a specific position at the time of exam. The page displays no update date; the date used is the Code's entry into force, June 12, 2017.

title: CCT No. 25: pay equality
summary: CCT No. 25 requires pay equality between women and men for equal work or work of equal value. The salary offered at hiring must respect this principle.
body: Article 2 frames scope by reference to the law of December 5, 1968 on CCTs. Article 3 requires elimination of sex-based discrimination in pay elements and conditions.

Evaluation systems must use criteria, weighting, and conversion to pay respecting equality. Sectors and companies must evaluate their classifications and correct them if necessary. To prepare an offer, verify the job class and justify salary differences by professional criteria.
Article 4 notably covers cash salary, money-valued benefits, and certain supplementary provisions. Thus check all pay offered. Coordinated version last modified by CCT No. 25 ter of July 9, 2008.

title: Language of personnel documents in Brussels
summary: In Brussels, Article 52 of the coordinated laws of July 18, 1966 governs the language of personnel documents of industrial, commercial, or financial companies. The worker's language must be considered.
body: Article 52, § 1, targets acts and documents required by law or regulations as well as those for personnel. In the Brussels-Capital Region, documents for French-speaking staff are drafted in French and those for Dutch-speaking staff in Dutch. The operating headquarters is determinative.
§ 2 authorizes additional translations when staff composition justifies, without replacing the required version. Article 59 provides for replacement of irregular documents.

When preparing hiring, verify the language of individual documents and contract. Article 52 does not, by itself, create a general obligation to publish every private posting in both languages. Public services follow other provisions of these laws.

title: Request the correct criminal record extract
summary: The SPF Justice describes the procedure for authorized employers. The request must match the activity and rest on applicable regulation.
body: The recruiter completes the form intended for the candidate and indicates the appropriate extract type. It distinguishes regulated activities and those falling under education, psycho-medical-social guidance, youth assistance, child protection, or supervision of minors, covered under Article 596, paragraph 2, of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The candidate then presents the form to his/her municipality, or to the Central Criminal Record when he/she has no domicile or residence in Belgium. The administration dates and signs the form and delivers the extract to the candidate.

The requested document contains only information relevant to the activity concerned. This procedure does not give all employers general authorization to check the background of every candidate. Communication published June 28, 2017.

title: Pay transparency: federal status in September 2026
summary: An analysis published September 17, 2026 notes the absence of federal transposition of Directive 2023/970. Do not present its deadline as a new obligation already applicable to all private Belgian employers.
body: The PKF BOFIDI Legal team indicates that as of September 17, 2026 no federal bill draft had been filed. The European deadline was June 7, 2026. This source documents a dated transposition status; it does not allow stating that no later change is possible.

The analysis distinguishes new transparency obligations, notably candidate information provided under Article 5, from already applicable rights. A directive does not by itself create obligations directly enforceable between individuals. Public sector and entity transpositions require separate verification.

The recruiter must already respect the Gender law and pay equality. Preparing objective salary criteria remains useful, but a notice intended for the private sector should not announce a universal federal obligation of salary range solely on the basis of the directive.

title: Prepare gender-neutral salary classifications
summary: The SPF Employment presents the BE-MAGIC analysis on classifications and the pay transparency directive. It helps prepare grids used in salary offers.
body: The publication of September 29, 2025 distinguishes the pay equality principle already set in European and Belgian law from adaptations necessary to transpose the directive. It does not constitute transposition text.

The project aims to provide social partners with tools for gender-neutral job classification and evaluation, within Article 4, paragraph 2, of the directive. For recruitment, tie the offered salary to the evaluated function and verify criterion neutrality.

The analysis also covers sectoral classifications and other salary benefits. It is useful for revising a grid but does not suffice to establish the timeline of new federal obligations in September 2026; consult the transposition notice.
